engine_name: llama.cpp (llama-server) — ggml-org/llama.cpp, builds b8738+ (reasoning fixes), per-request reasoning budget visible from commit 0fcb3760; core reasoning-budget sampler merged via acb7c790 around build b8850 (April 2026). Serving unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF UD-Q4_K_XL (18.8 GB).
cuda_128_compatible: Yes. llama.cpp builds cleanly against CUDA 12.8 on sm_86 (A6000). Pre-built CUDA binaries are published on the GitHub releases page (llama-bXXXX-bin-ubuntu-cuda-x64.zip), and a pip wheel exists via the llama-cpp-python project (CUDA build via CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_CUDA=on"). For the standalone llama-server binary used here, source compilation is simple: clone repo, `cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`, then `cmake --build build --config Release -j`. Build complexity is LOW; CUDA 12.x (including 12.8) is fully supported. [uncertain on exact wheel availability for the very latest b8800+ builds]
gemma4_support: Yes — Gemma 4 (dense 31B thinking model) is supported. Required format is GGUF. Quants are available on HuggingFace: unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF (UD-Q4_K_XL = 18.8 GB, the one in use) and unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-GGUF. The model uses Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with a fixed ~3.6 GB SWA KV cache that must be budgeted. Gemma-4-specific gaps as of 2026: (a) per-request enable_thinking toggle is silently ignored (template/parser bug); (b) the MTP assistant/drafter architecture (Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM) is NOT yet recognized by convert_hf_to_gguf.py on upstream master, so speculative decoding with the official MTP draft does not work on stock builds; (c) F16 GGUF on CUDA can produce a <unused49> token flood when thinking is active (quantized quants like Q4_K are unaffected).
per_request_reasoning_toggle: PARTIALLY. The per-request OpenAI-style fields are unreliable for Gemma 4 on llama-server: chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} is silently IGNORED for Gemma 4 (server log still shows thinking=1, output still contains reasoning). reasoning_effort: 'none' / reasoning: {effort: 'none'} are NOT supported by llama-server at all. The reliable controls are SERVER-LEVEL flags, not per-request: `--reasoning off` (-rea off) is the confirmed working fix for Gemma 4 (works from build b8738, ~5x speedup with no reasoning output). `--reasoning-budget 0` is supposed to fully disable thinking but was reported NOT to work on Gemma 4 in several builds. So per-request ON/OFF toggling of thinking does not work reliably for Gemma 4 — only a global server flag does.
per_request_reasoning_budget: Yes — the per-request parameter is `thinking_budget_tokens` (request body: {"thinking_budget_tokens": N}). CRITICAL CONSTRAINT confirmed in source: it is only honored when the server-side `--reasoning-budget` flag is NOT set, because the code path is `if (reasoning_budget == -1 && body.contains("thinking_budget_tokens"))` (server-common.cpp ~lines 1107-1119, commit 0fcb3760). If you pass --reasoning-budget N on the command line, the global value wins and the per-request field is ignored — this is exactly the reported failure mode. FIX for the planner-vs-tool-dispatch shared-budget problem: do NOT set --reasoning-budget as a server flag; leave it at default -1, then send thinking_budget_tokens per request (large budget for the planner node, small/0 for the tool-dispatch node). The budget is enforced by a sampler state machine (IDLE->COUNTING->WAITING_UTF8->FORCING->DONE) operating between the thinking start/end tags; pair it with --reasoning-budget-message to avoid abrupt mid-sentence cutoff at the hard token limit. Note: thinking_budget_tokens=0 may not fully suppress thinking on Gemma 4 the way --reasoning off does, due to the same template bug affecting toggling.
tool_calling_support: llama-server handles Gemma 4 tool/function calling via `--jinja` with the model's embedded Gemma 4 chat template (the current serve command already uses --jinja). It exposes OpenAI-compatible tools/tool_choice. There is no separate '--tool-call-parser gemma4' flag like vLLM has; llama.cpp relies on the Jinja chat template plus its grammar-constrained / template-driven parsing. Known Gemma-4 failure modes reported in 2026: template/parser issues causing the <unused49> flood (F16 on CUDA), and reasoning-tag handling interacting with tool-call delimiters. Streaming partial tool calls and multi-turn tool use generally work but are less battle-tested than vLLM's dedicated gemma4 parser. [uncertain on current streaming tool-call reliability specifics for Gemma 4]
openai_api_compatible: Yes. llama-server exposes /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions with SSE streaming, compatible with openai-python and httpx asyncio clients. Deviations to note: reasoning content is returned in message.reasoning_content only when --reasoning-format deepseek (default 'auto'); with --reasoning-format none thoughts stay in message.content. reasoning_effort is not supported. Non-standard extension fields like thinking_budget_tokens and chat_template_kwargs are accepted in the request body. Otherwise the schema matches OpenAI closely enough for standard async clients.
continuous_batching: Yes. llama-server supports continuous batching / parallel slots via --parallel N (current command uses --parallel 2). It serves multiple concurrent requests without full serialization. For a small local agent (max 10 concurrent users, 4-8 parallel sub-agents) this is adequate; increase --parallel and ensure enough KV cache VRAM per slot. Note each parallel slot reserves its own SWA KV; for a sole user, -np 1 reserves a single SWA KV instead of the default, saving significant VRAM. llama.cpp's batching is functional but less throughput-optimized than vLLM's PagedAttention continuous batching; for the stated small scale it is sufficient.
installation_steps:
Host-native build on CUDA 12.8 (Ubuntu/Debian RunPod pod):
  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake git libcurl4-openssl-dev
  git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp
  cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86 -DLLAMA_CURL=ON
  cmake --build build --config Release -j$(nproc)
  # binary at ./build/bin/llama-server
Use a recent build (>= b8738) so the Gemma 4 `--reasoning off` fix and per-request thinking_budget_tokens are present. Alternatively download the pre-built CUDA release binary from the GitHub releases page (llama-bXXXX-bin-ubuntu-cuda-x64.zip) to skip compilation. Model: `huggingface-cli download unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF gemma-4-31B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --local-dir ./models`.
serve_command:
llama-server \
  -m models/gemma-4-31B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --jinja \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 \
  --ctx-size 16384 \
  --parallel 2 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  -fa on \
  --reasoning-format deepseek \
  --reasoning-budget-message "\n</think>\n"
  # IMPORTANT: do NOT pass --reasoning-budget N — leaving it at default (-1) is what enables
  #   per-request {"thinking_budget_tokens": N} so the planner and tool-dispatch nodes can have
  #   independent budgets. If you instead want thinking globally OFF, add `--reasoning off`
  #   (this is the only reliable per-Gemma-4 disable; enable_thinking:false per request is ignored).
  # For a single user, add `-np 1` to reserve only one SWA KV slot and save VRAM.
Per-request body example (planner): {"messages":[...],"thinking_budget_tokens":2048}
Per-request body example (tool dispatch): {"messages":[...],"thinking_budget_tokens":0}
speculative_decoding: Partially / NOT on stock builds for the official MTP draft. llama-server supports generic speculative decoding via --draft-model / -md plus --draft-max and --draft-min. HOWEVER, the official Gemma 4 MTP drafter (mtp-gemma-4-31B / Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM) is NOT supported on upstream master: convert_hf_to_gguf.py throws 'unknown model architecture: gemma4_assistant', and --draft-model with a Gemma 4 MTP GGUF does not work on stock builds. Tracking: discussion #22735, WIP PR #23398. Working paths today: (a) reffdev/llama.cpp 'gemma4-mtp' fork (functional but not PR-quality; --spec-draft-n-max/--spec-draft-p-min are ineffective there, draft capacity clamped to 5); (b) pre-converted GGUFs at AtomicChat/gemma-4-assistant-gguf; (c) newer experimental builds auto-discover the MTP drafter from -hf via `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 -ngl 999 -fa on`. Expected speedup once working: Google claims up to 2x; community measured ~1.7-1.9x on short/code generations, 70-87% draft acceptance, up to ~60% throughput gain. On A6000 48GB the 0.5 GB MTP draft adds negligible VRAM, so the trade-off is favorable IF support lands. Recommended --draft-max 6-8 for code; smaller for creative text. [uncertain — exact A6000 tok/s not benchmarked in sources; feature not yet merged upstream]
known_issues_gemma4: 1) enable_thinking:false (per-request, chat_template_kwargs) silently ignored on Gemma 4 — log shows thinking=1; use server flag --reasoning off instead (discussion #21338, confirmed working b8738). 2) --reasoning-budget 0 reported NOT to disable thinking on Gemma 4 in several builds. 3) Per-request thinking_budget_tokens is ignored if --reasoning-budget is set on the command line (reasoning_budget must be -1) — discussion #21445. 4) <unused49> token flood specific to F16 GGUF on CUDA when thinking active (reasoning_content empty, finish_reason length); quantized quants (Q4_K_M, the UD-Q4_K_XL in use) are unaffected — builds b8638/b8672. 5) Gemma 4 MTP speculative decoding unsupported on upstream master (discussion #22735, PR #23398 WIP). 6) Reasoning-budget sampler defaulting to INT_MAX after April-2026 builds caused non-deterministic indefinite hangs unless a cap/--reasoning off is set (forge issue #54). 7) High SWA KV-cache VRAM and slow prefill (attention on nearly all layers) are inherent Gemma 4 characteristics.
vram_usage: UD-Q4_K_XL weights ~18.8 GB on disk / ~21 GB resident in VRAM. Plus a fixed ~3.6 GB SWA KV cache. At 16,384 context: measured ~22.3 GB total in llama.cpp at FP16 KV (one slot). With --parallel 2, KV roughly doubles for the non-SWA portion. On a 48 GB A6000 at 16k context this leaves comfortable headroom (~20+ GB free) — enough to co-resident BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (0.13 GB) and BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 (2.3 GB). With unquantized KV, ~32k context fills ~48 GB; for 16k there is ample room. Use -np 1 (single SWA KV) if sole user to reclaim VRAM. KV quantization (Q8_0/Q4_0 via -ctk/-ctv, requires -fa) further reduces KV footprint substantially if longer context is needed.
small_scale_fit: Strong fit. llama.cpp is the simplest viable engine for 1 developer + max 10 concurrent users, and it is the stated current baseline. Host-native, no containers, single static binary, trivial config, runs the existing GGUF directly. Operational overhead is the lowest of any option; portability to future personal A6000-class hardware is excellent (same binary + GGUF). The only friction is the Gemma 4 reasoning-control quirks (use --reasoning off or per-request thinking_budget_tokens without the server flag) and the not-yet-merged MTP speculative decoding. For the stated scale, these are minor and the simplicity strongly justifies staying on llama.cpp.
overall_recommendation: RECOMMENDED (as the current baseline). It satisfies every hard constraint: CUDA 12.8 / A6000 sm_86 supported, runs the existing UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF, OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with SSE, host-native no containers, low ops overhead, fits 16k context on 48 GB with room for embedder+reranker. PROS: simplest deployment, the per-request reasoning-budget problem is SOLVABLE — leave --reasoning-budget unset (default -1) and send thinking_budget_tokens per request so the planner and tool-dispatch nodes get independent budgets (the exact fix the task was after); -fa on gives ~40% KV VRAM savings and speed with comparable quality on typical tasks. CONS / WATCH-OUTS: per-request enable_thinking toggle is silently ignored for Gemma 4 (must use global --reasoning off for a hard off); official MTP speculative decoding is not yet merged upstream (PR #23398 WIP) so the ~1.7-2x speedup is not available on stock builds today; tool-calling lacks a dedicated parser (relies on --jinja template) and is less hardened than vLLM's gemma4 parser. Net: keep llama.cpp; pin a build >= b8738, do not set --reasoning-budget, drive reasoning per request via thinking_budget_tokens, enable -fa on, and revisit speculative decoding when PR #23398 merges.
